name: tipping.elements
summary: The climate tipping elements from data/events/tipping.toml, each with the global warming at which an assessment judged it likely to tip (a central estimate and a range) and its timescale, checked every year against the run's global anomaly. A tipping.crossing event the first year the run passes an element's low end and again its central estimate. The table is the claim; the module only compares. With coupling above zero the file's coupling rows act: once an element has passed its threshold, the elements it is coupled to have their thresholds lowered by the row's fraction times the strength, so one crossing can bring the next within reach in the same run (Wunderling et al. 2021: interacting elements lower each other's critical temperatures, the ice sheets start cascades, the Atlantic circulation carries them).

params.name: coupling
params.note: 0: each element is checked against the warming alone (the runs before 2026-11-07); 1: the full fractional shifts in the coupling rows, which are the paper's ensemble-mean lowering at its full interaction strength; between, a scaled share. The shifted thresholds apply to every level and to the carbon module downstream

name: carbon.tipped
summary: The first cascade: a tipping element past its threshold releases the carbon its row of data/events/tipping.toml states, on the row's timescale, into the carbon ledger, where the pools module treats it as it treats fossil carbon, so the warming it adds comes back through the same energy balance. Three elements carry a carbon table from Armstrong McKay et al. 2022: boreal permafrost abrupt thaw (per degree, declining), Amazon partial dieback (30 GtC), boreal permafrost collapse (125 GtC). Each year the mass still owed is released as a first-order approach over the element's timescale. Nothing is modelled here; the amounts, thresholds and timescales are the assessment's and the module only moves the stated mass over the stated time.

The one response by people is the capacity module's, where a variant turns it on: the planned cut slowed by what the heat and the shocks do, under a placeholder rule. Of the tipping elements, only the carbon of permafrost and the Amazon feeds back, and only once the run passes the assessment's thresholds; the rest are flags. The population here is the UN's path, which assumes none of the above changes where people live. Every crossing above is a count of people living where a stated limit is passed, not a toll, and the model runs about 0.15 °C warm in 2024. The warming applied to a place is its country's, from the country record scaled by the run's global anomaly: wherever something has held a country's warming back so far, this holds it back still, and within a country the pattern of the recent past is held.

name: fire.cells
summary: Our own fire engine: a heat budget on one-arc-second cells that know their elevation and slope, land cover, the share under buildings and their height, the major roads, and the hour's 3 km wind, gust, temperature and humidity. A burning cell radiates heat into the cells around it, further downwind and upslope; a cell ignites when the heat it has received outweighs what its fuel and moisture absorb, then burns with the intensity and for the time its contents set; strong winds loft embers that may start spot fires; roads and water carry nothing; nobody fights it. Every rate and threshold is a guess, declared so, to be fitted against the record.

name: score.regions
summary: A score per country in nine bands (living, means, fairness, voice, air, forest, protected, water, footprint), each a World Bank indicator turned into a 0 to 1 percentile rank among the countries that report it, so a band says where a country stands among its peers and never what a good number is; the total is the mean of the bands it has. The starting state is read from the record. From the run's first year the bands move by declared placeholder rules: a country whose people pass the heat thresholds loses part of its living and water bands, and a wild card knocks a band for some years by its kind. Published as a table for the globe view: the glyph at each country's centroid is the bands stacked, the total its height.
dt: 1 year (1 January); the table published every every_years, and every every_years_after from from_year

params.name: scale
params.note: Natural Earth scale for the country list and centroids

params.name: every_years
params.note: how often the table is published before from_year

params.name: from_year
params.note: from this year the table is published every every_years_after

params.name: every_years_after
params.note: the cadence from from_year; each table is about 40 KB in the log, so the cadence is the page's weight

params.name: stress_living
params.note: the living band is multiplied by one minus this times the country's heat stress, the larger of the share of its people past the climate niche and the share past the 31 °C wet-bulb limit (a guess)

params.name: stress_water
params.note: the water band, by one minus this times the share past the niche (a guess)

params.name: stress_means
params.note: the means band, by one minus this times the heat stress (a guess)

subscribes.note: { kind, forcing_years, emissions_years } a wild card knocks a band for some years by its kind: disease the living band, economy and technology the means, war the living and the voice, an eruption or an impact the air, an ecological card the water and the forest (all guesses, all global)

views.title: mean total score
views.note: the plain mean over countries, not weighted by people; the globe itself is drawn at the top of the page by the story module

assets.note: the nine indicators, latest value per country

notes: The ranks are among the countries that report an indicator, so a country missing a band is not penalised and its total is the mean of what it has. Every rule that moves a band after the first year is a placeholder written on 2026-11-05 and declared in the parameters; the indicators themselves are read, not modelled, and their years differ by band (the table on the run page names each). The heat stress is the run's own: the share of a country's people living in cells past the niche or the wet-bulb limit this year, read from the heat and wet-bulb modules' fields, so it rises as the run warms and needs no crossing. A mean cannot say a country is failing, since a gating pressure (heat on its people, water, food, the sea) is not averaged away by wealth; the stress is published beside the total for that reason, and the globe reads it first.

name: policy.capacity
summary: Derailment: the world's capacity to cut emissions, 0 to 1, eroded by what the run's own warming does to people and recovering slowly, after Dyke (The Conversation, 2026-11-05): the consequences of climate change erode the capacity to address its causes, through debt, conflict and backlash, and collective action is easier to destroy than to build. Each January the capacity moves toward a target set by the share of people under heat stress (from the regions module), amplified where the people-weighted fairness band is low; it falls fast and recovers slowly, the recovery scaled by the voice band; a wild card knocks it by its kind for some years; and where a country's people are under stress a conflict may be drawn, which takes a fraction of that country's people and knocks the capacity by the country's share of the world. With mode = on the capacity goes to the emissions module, which slows every planned cut by it: a plan to zero by 2050 becomes zero by later or never. Beside it, the options: the carbon budget left to a stated warming level under a stated TCRE and the cut rate now needed to hold it, from the run's own series. Every number here is a placeholder and says so; the shape is the article's and the inputs are the run's.
dt: 1 year (1 January), after the regions module

params.name: mode
params.note: off: nothing happens; watch: the capacity and the options are computed and reported, nothing is changed; on: the capacity is published to the emissions module and conflicts are drawn

params.name: gain
params.note: the target capacity is one minus gain times the share of the world's people under heat stress (a guess: at today's 2% that is 0.92, at a fifth of everyone 0.2)

params.name: inequality
params.note: the pressure is multiplied by one plus this times one minus the people-weighted fairness band (the article: conflict and backlash are stronger where inequality is high; a guess)

params.name: fall
params.note: the share of the gap to a lower target closed each year (fast)

params.name: recover
params.note: the share of the gap to a higher target closed each year, times the people-weighted voice band (slow; the article's asymmetry)

params.name: floor
params.note: the capacity never falls below this

params.name: knock_economy
params.note: a financial or technology wild card multiplies the capacity by one minus this for its emissions_years (a guess)

params.name: knock_war
params.note: a war wild card, for five years (a guess)

params.name: knock_disease
params.note: a pandemic wild card, for three years (a guess)

params.name: knock_eruption
params.note: a cooling eruption or impact, for its forcing_years (a guess)

params.name: conflict_gain
params.note: a country's annual chance of conflict is this times the share of its people under heat stress, times one plus inequality times one minus its fairness band, times one minus half its voice band (a guess; mode = on only)

params.name: conflict_mortality
params.note: the fraction of that country's people a conflict takes, once (a guess)

params.name: conflict_knock
params.note: the world capacity is multiplied by one minus this for every percent of the world's people in the country, capped at 0.2, for conflict_years (a guess)

params.name: level_c
params.note: the warming level the options are measured against

params.name: level2_c
params.note: a second, higher level, for when the first is spent

params.name: tcre_c_per_gtc
params.note: transient climate response to cumulative emissions: AR6's best estimate of 0.45 °C per 1000 GtCO2, which is 1.65e-3 °C per GtC (recalled, not checked against the report)

params.name: from
params.note: no change before this date, so the hindcast is untouched

views.title: capacity to cut emissions
views.note: one is the plan as written; what the heat, the wild cards and the conflicts leave of it

views.title: the cut now needed to hold 2 °C
views.note: percent a year from this year on, on a straight line to zero that spends the budget exactly; 100 when nothing is left

views.title: the cut now needed to hold 3 °C
views.note: the same, for the higher level

views.title: carbon budget left to 2 °C
views.note: under the stated TCRE, from the run's own warming

notes: The budget left is (level_c minus the run's warming) over the TCRE, in GtC, and zero once the level is passed; the years left are that over last year's emissions; the cut now needed is the constant percentage fall from today that spends exactly the budget on a straight line to zero, which is half the current rate over the budget, capped at 100 when nothing is left. The capacity applies to the planned fall only: a held or growing path is not helped by a weak capacity, and a lost year of cutting is not recovered when the capacity returns, which is the article's point. Conflicts here are a draw from the run's seed where the heat stress is, not a forecast of any war.
